title: Embeddings & Similarity, Honestly
objective: After this lesson you will be able to explain what embeddings capture (and miss), compute cosine similarity, choose embedding granularity (query vs chunk symmetry), and keep a TF-IDF baseline that justifies every upgrade.
why: Embeddings feel magical until they fail: 'reimbursement' matches 'refund' beautifully, then SKU 'SH-1-v9' matches nothing and prices collide semantically. Understanding vectors as *lossy meaning projections* — brilliant at paraphrase, blind to exact tokens — determines chunk design, hybrid strategy, and when the baseline beats the upgrade. No linear algebra worship; just working mental models with numbers.

blocks.text: An **embedding** maps text to a dense vector where related meanings sit nearby. **Cosine similarity** (angle, not length) scores closeness: 1 identical direction, 0 orthogonal, −1 opposed. What they capture: paraphrase, synonyms, topical aboutness. What they miss: exact tokens (SKUs, IDs, numbers), negation scope, and fine distinctions the training never emphasized. Lossy in known directions — design around the losses.

blocks.caption: Angle measures meaning overlap; toy vectors show the geometry, not real scores

blocks.text: Retrieval compares query vectors against chunk vectors — both must come from **compatible encoders** (same model, or vendor-matched pairs). Asymmetric setups (short queries vs long chunks) benefit from instruction prefixes ('Represent this query for retrieval:') where supported. Mismatched encoders produce confident nonsense: similarity scores without shared geometry are random numbers with decimals.

Keep the OpenDataLoader TF-IDF baseline running beside embeddings: per-query, record both rankings. Upgrade justified only on measured miss-swaps (lexical misses fixed > semantic misses introduced) *minus* cost delta. Teams that delete baselines lose the ability to say whether embeddings helped — and on SKU-heavy catalogs, they often haven't.

blocks.title: Feel the geometry
blocks.note: Run it: expect paraphrase ≈0.996, sku ≈0.006, self ≈1 (0.9999999999999999 — floating-point dust on the sqrt round-trip; real code compares with epsilon, never ===). Toy vectors demonstrate geometry (nearby vs orthogonal vs identical) — real embeddings show the same three relationships on real text.

items: Cosine scores direction overlap: paraphrase-near, exact-tokens-orthogonal, identical-one
Encoder compatibility is load-bearing: mismatched spaces produce confident nonsense
TF-IDF baselines justify upgrades per-query: miss-swaps minus cost, measured always

exercise.prompt: (a) Run the practice geometry and record all three scores. (b) Add a fourth vector 'returns' = [0.7, 0.3, 0.1] and rank all three against 'refund' — state the order with scores. (c) In one sentence each: when embeddings beat TF-IDF on your catalog, and when TF-IDF beats embeddings.
hints: Baseline: 0.996 / 0.006 / 1. Ranked addition slots by angle: returns lands between paraphrase and SKU (compute exactly).
Embeddings win: paraphrase-heavy shopper language ('comfy long-distance shoes' → cushioning copy). TF-IDF wins: SKUs, exact model numbers, prices.
Both sentences name miss profiles, not vibes: lexical gaps vs semantic blur.
exercise.why: Ranking by angle on controlled vectors builds geometric intuition cheaply; the two sentences convert intuition into corpus-specific policy (which queries route where — preview of hybrid Ch.4).
exercise.code: // Geometry probe pattern: controlled vectors → ranked angles → policy sentences.

options: Exact-token blindness: vectors blur SKUs/IDs — lexical rescue (TF-IDF/BM25/metadata filter) required alongside
quiz.explain: Lossy projections sacrifice exact tokens for meaning. SKU/ID queries need lexical paths — the hybrid motivation (Ch.4).

quiz.q: Query and chunk embedded with different models. Result?
options: Confident nonsense: similarities without shared geometry are meaningless decimals — encoder compatibility is load-bearing
quiz.explain: Vector spaces aren't interchangeable. Cross-encoder comparisons score noise; matched pairs (or vendor-matched asymmetric setups) only.

quiz.q: Team deleted the TF-IDF baseline after adopting embeddings. Cost?
options: Lost measurability: no per-query miss-swap accounting, so upgrade value becomes faith — keep baselines running
quiz.explain: Baselines price upgrades: lexical misses fixed vs semantic misses introduced, minus cost. Deleted baselines make regressions undetectable.

summary: Cosine geometry (near/orthogonal/identical), encoder compatibility, baselines that price upgrades. Vectors project meaning lossily — design for the losses.
next: Meaning plus terms beats either alone: fusing lexical and vector retrieval with discipline. Next: hybrid retrieval.
